E-commerce Logistics Fulfillment Ecosystem for WeChat Store: a B2B2C experience architecture from zero to one

Multi-role architecture; Cross-platform experience; Project management Apr 2026 ~20 min read

Context

In its early stages, WeChat Channels Shop (WeChat Store) only supported fulfillment via self-shipping and electronic waybills.

For Merchants:

  • Low shipping efficiency;
  • Heavy reliance on offline communication;
  • Tedious hardware configuration;
  • Small-and-medium (SMB) merchants lacked bargaining power for logistics price.

For the Platform:

  • Uncontrollable logistics service quality;
  • Lack of standardized fulfillment metrics.

For Buyers:

  • High risk of data leaks, as merchants were forced to decrypt personal delivery information for self-shipping.

Challenge

  • Build from 0 to 1: Designing a B2B2C fulfillment system from scratch to support complex business workflows.
  • Connect 4 roles & 5 product lines: Designing for 4 types of users (Buyers/Merchants/Logistics Providers/Suppliers) and linking 5 product lines (Logistics, Orders, etc.).
  • Covering both Mobile and PC, ensuring a highly efficient and intuitive workflow for all users.

My role

  • Owned the 0-to-1 core framework; turned complex B2B2C logistics into a simple, intuitive product.
  • Collaborate with Product Managers to formulate strategy, and align with the development team regarding technical constraints to ensure the successful delivery of the product.
  • Mentored and led one full-time designer, breaking down complex tasks to ensure high-quality delivery.

Phase 2: Focus on core capabilities, transitioning from "integrated supply and sales" to "separated supply and sales""

With the development of e-commerce business, after the scale of small stores expands, the merchant system gradually shifts from "integrated supply and sales" to "separation of supply and sales":

  • Merchants: Focus on product sales and store operations
  • Supplier: provides goods and is responsible for shipping

Phase 2: De-coupling Supply & Sales"

Efficient Order Assignment

To improve the efficiency of merchants in allocating orders while retaining a certain ability to correct errors, 3 allocation methods are provided:

  • Manual Assignment
  • Product-Based Auto-Assignment
  • Store-Wide Auto-Assignment

Manual Assignment: fallback method, retain error correction capability, improve system fault tolerance

Product-Based Auto-Assignment: Rules-based workflows to automatically dispatch orders by specific products.

Store-Wide Auto-Assignment: Fully-automated workflows that instantly route all store orders to a default supplier.
